instr: Six sentences from a meeting about a course. Match each one to what the speaker is doing.

itens.t: "The document allocates twenty hours to the unit."
itens.porque: Quoting: you can point at the line. Everything else in this list adds something the document does not contain.

itens.t: "So somebody changed it after it was approved."
itens.porque: A conclusion, and a reasonable one — but neither document says it. Say it in the same tone as the line above and the coordinator cannot tell them apart.

itens.t: "Who signs this off -- you or the head of studies?"
itens.porque: Asking for a decision. Not a finding: the finding is that a decision is missing.

itens.t: "I would leave the assessment where the syllabus has it."
itens.porque: A recommendation. It belongs at the END of the briefing, after the divergences — put first, it turns a report into an argument.

itens.t: "Sorry -- is that week seven or week eight?"
itens.porque: Checking a fact. It costs three seconds and prevents the rest of the briefing from resting on the wrong number.

itens.t: "That is in the plan, not in the syllabus."
itens.porque: Correcting — and this is the sentence the whole lesson is built on: the claim arrives with its source attached.

nota.texto:
Every one of them will happen in the lesson. The difference between the first two is
      the whole point of the lesson: one can be checked against the page, the other cannot.

instr: Complete each sentence so that the source arrives **with** the claim, not after it.
itens: "{The syllabus says} twenty hours, and the plan has eighteen."
"{According to the plan} , the assessment is in week seven."
"These two {do not line up} on who corrects the writing."
"{My reading is} that nobody reread the syllabus."

itens.t: How long the unit runs
itens.porque: Both say it, and they disagree: eighteen against twenty. A divergence, not a gap.

itens.t: Why the report is corrected by a classmate
itens.porque: Neither says why. The plan says it happens; nobody explains the choice — and that is what you ask for.

itens.t: When the assessment happens
itens.porque: Both say it, and they disagree (week seven against week eight).

itens.t: How long the written report is
itens.porque: It is in the documents. Not a gap.

itens.t: Whether anyone approved these choices
itens.porque: A real gap, and the most important one: without it, nobody knows whether these are decisions or drift.

itens.t: What the listening task is built on
itens.porque: The plan describes the task. What is missing is the SOURCE it is built on — but that is detail, not the gap that changes the decision.

sec4.rationale: The plan says what will happen. It never says why, and it never says who agreed to it -- and that is normal for a plan.
abertura: Read the lesson plan. Nothing else -- you are not comparing anything yet.

abertura.texto:
Unit 7 runs over 18 teaching hours, from week 5 to week 7. The unit closes with a
      written report of 180–220 words. The report is corrected by a classmate against the
      checklist on page 4, and then rewritten once; the teacher reads the rewritten version.
      The unit assessment is in week 7, in the last session. There is a listening task in
      session 4 built on a recorded staff meeting; it is not assessed.

abertura: Mark the **two** things the plan does **not** tell you.

alts: to spend all of it before the end
to set aside a fixed amount of it for a purpose
itens.ok: to set aside a fixed amount of it for a purpose

itens.t: to run beyond something
alts: to go past the limit that was set
itens.ok: to go past the limit that was set

alts: something you have promised and can be held to
itens.ok: something you have promised and can be held to

alts: to be given to, as a share
itens.ok: to be given to, as a share

itens.ok: official permission from someone above you

alts: to suggest it without saying it
to say it clearly and on the record
itens.ok: to say it clearly and on the record

abertura: Choose the better meaning for each expression. You will meet all six in the two documents.

itens.t: It is written by a teacher
itens.porque: Both are. Who wrote it does not separate them — what they are FOR does.

itens.t: People outside the classroom rely on it
itens.porque: The syllabus. Coordination, the next teacher and the student read it, which is why it cannot be changed alone.

itens.t: It says what will happen in one session
itens.porque: That is the lesson plan. The syllabus covers the course.

itens.t: Changing it needs someone else to agree
itens.porque: The syllabus, again for the same reason: other people depend on it.

itens.t: It can be adjusted while the course runs
itens.porque: The plan. Adjusting it is normal work; adjusting the syllabus is a decision.

itens.t: It lists every task the students will do
itens.porque: Neither, and the syllabus says so explicitly. That line is what makes the missing listening task NOT a divergence.

sec1.rationale: A syllabus is a commitment: it is read by people who were not in the room, and it is not the teacher's to change alone. A plan is an instrument for one lesson.
abertura: Two documents describe the same course. One is a lesson plan; the other is the syllabus the course was sold with.
Mark the **two** statements that are true of a course syllabus and not of a lesson plan.

itens.titulo: How to Survive Your Next Observed Lesson
itens.fonte: TEFL Training Institute Podcast · with Matt Courtois
itens.texto: Fifteen minutes, two speakers, natural pace. They talk about being observed and about what happens in the conversation afterwards — which is the lesson you have in four weeks’ time.

abertura: Two teacher trainers talking about the situation on the other side of your job.

itens.titulo: Syllabus design (and a bit about coursebooks)
itens.texto: It opens with the question this lesson turned on: what is a syllabus, and how does it differ from a course plan? Written for teachers, in plain English.

abertura: Written for teachers, about the two kinds of document you worked with.
A quick reference to the situation and the language you used.

tabela: A short briefing to a coordinator who has read neither of two documents that should agree.
Naming where the two stop agreeing, and saying which document each claim comes from.
The syllabus says… · According to the plan,… · That comes from…, not from…
These two do not line up on… · One says X, the other says Y.
My reading is that… · Neither of them actually says it, but…
to allocate · to run beyond · a commitment · approval · to state something

callout.texto:
Before any sentence, ask one question: could someone with the document in front of them disagree with this?
If no, say it flat — it is a quotation. If yes, mark it as yours.

abertura: Record a short voice message, if you would like to.

callout.texto:
Think of two documents in your own school that are supposed to agree — a plan and a syllabus, a syllabus and a coursebook map, a course description and what is actually taught.

What you are trying to do: tell a colleague what does not line up, in a way she could repeat to someone else without checking.

lista: what each document is, in one sentence;
one point where they stop agreeing, and where each side of it is written;
one thing you concluded that neither document actually says;
what you think should be decided, and by whom.

abertura: Use this whenever you want to review what you did in class.

tabela: Without the source, a fact sounds like an opinion, and the other person has nothing to check.
My reading is that… · Putting the two together,…
Unmarked, your conclusion is heard as something the document says — and someone will look for it.
Unmarked, it sounds like a decision that has already been taken.

recurso.texto: The expression you used most in class, with its two meanings and example sentences.

itens.t: A unit that needs more hours than it was given
itens.porque: Approval from coordination. This is the line that turns the eighteen-against-twenty difference into something someone has to decide.

itens.t: The end-of-unit written work
itens.porque: The syllabus says the teacher corrects it. The plan gives it to a classmate — the second divergence, in one sentence.

itens.t: A task that this document does not mention
itens.ok: may still be used in class
alts: may still be used in class
itens.porque: May still be used. This is the trap defused: the listening task in the plan is not a divergence, because the syllabus never claimed to list everything.

abertura: Now the syllabus. Again on its own.

doc.texto:
The semester is divided into four units. Unit 7 is allocated 20 teaching hours, and no
      unit may run beyond its allocation without approval from the coordination. Written work
      produced at the end of a unit is corrected by the teacher, with written feedback
      returned to the student within one week. Each unit is assessed in the week after it
      ends. This syllabus states what the course commits to; it does not list every task a
      teacher may use.
doc.titulo: Course syllabus -- General English B1, second semester

nota.titulo: “It does not list every task” is the line to hold on to
nota.texto:
A document that does not claim to list everything is not disagreeing with a document
      that lists more. You will need that distinction in class.
